name: Chat with your CSV and Excel data using Claude and a free Cradler database

parameters.content:
## Chat with your CSV and Excel data, no database to set up

Upload a CSV or Excel file and ask questions about it in plain words: "How many orders are unpaid?", "Which category had the most refunds?", "Revenue from paid orders in September?". The file goes into a free [Cradler](https://cradler.ai) database, which creates the table and columns on the first write, and an AI agent running Claude through [apimodels.app](https://apimodels.app) looks up the table, queries it and does the math.

### How it works
1. **Upload form** takes the file and a table name. Headers become snake_case columns and each column gets one type (number, true/false or text).
2. Rows are inserted in batches of 500, and the table is recorded in a `data_tables` list.
3. In the **Chat**, the agent lists tables, reads a table's columns, then runs read-only queries with filters, sorting and exact counts, and uses the calculator for sums and averages.

### Setup
1. Create a free project at [cradler.ai](https://cradler.ai) and add its **service** key as a **Bearer Auth** credential named "Cradler service key".
2. Create an API key in the [apimodels console](https://apimodels.app/console/api-keys) and add an **OpenAI** credential with Base URL `https://api.apimodels.app/v1`.
3. In **Settings**, replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your Cradler project id.
4. Activate, upload a file through the form, then open the chat from the **Chat** node.
Step-by-step guide: [apimodels.app/docs/n8n](https://apimodels.app/docs/n8n)

### Good to know
- One query returns at most 1,000 rows, so sums and averages are exact up to that many matching rows; counts are always exact. Best for files up to a few thousand rows.
- The chat tools can only read data. Keep both forms private or behind Basic Auth.

## 1. Import a file
Reads CSV or Excel, cleans headers and types, inserts in batches and records the table.

## 2. Chat with the data
The agent lists tables, reads columns, runs read-only queries and calculates.

parameters.formDescription: Upload a CSV or Excel file. The first row must contain the column names.

parameters.initialMessages:
Hi! Ask me anything about the data you uploaded.
For example: "How many orders are unpaid?"

options.title: Chat with your data
options.subtitle: Read-only answers from your Cradler tables

options.systemMessage:
You answer questions about tabular data stored in a Cradler database. Your tools are read-only.
1. Call list_tables to see which tables exist, their columns and row counts.
2. Call get_table_schema for the table you need.
3. Call query_table with a request object: select (column list), filters (field, op, value; ops: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, in, is_null), order (field, desc), limit (1 to 1000) and count "exact".
For "how many" questions use count "exact" with limit 1 and read total. For sums, averages, minimums or maximums, select only the needed column with limit 1000, then use the calculator on the returned values. If total is larger than the rows returned, say the answer covers only the first 1000 matching rows. Dates are stored as text such as 2026-09-14, so filter a month with gte "2026-09-01" and lt "2026-10-01". Use ilike for case-insensitive text matches. Answer briefly with the number first, then one line on how you got it. Never invent numbers; if the data cannot answer the question, say so.
